Alright, the user wants a "refinement pass over everything" with perfect visual quality, black/white menus, ultra fancy fonts, animations—essentially a full polish. I've already made several substantial changes:

1. Updated the CSS to an obsidian theme with black backgrounds, white text, custom fonts, shadows, etc.
2. Modified index.html to preload Google Fonts for Fredoka and Inter.
3. Exported `buildHat` in player.js so it can be imported elsewhere.
4. Created a new `hatthumb.js` module to render 3D hat thumbnails.
5. Added tone mapping settings to the renderer in `world.js`.
6. Added a note that I will continue with engine fixes: tone mapping, sun target, sun follow, death flash, studio grid.

Now I need to keep moving forward with the engine fixes. The next item in my plan is to make the directional light representing the sun actually track the player. In the current `world.js`, the sun is created as a `THREE.DirectionalLight` and added to the scene, but its `target` is never added to the scene graph. Without adding `sun.target` to the scene, the light's direction cannot be updated relative to a target object (like the player). This can cause the lighting to appear static or incorrect when the player moves, which is a visual glitch the user will notice.

I recall that earlier I added code to update the sun’s position each frame based on the player’s location (the "sun follow" fix). However, that code only manipulates `sun.position` and perhaps `sun.target.position`, but if the target isn’t part of the scene, the directional light won’t correctly orient. To fix this, I need to insert a line that adds `sun.target` to the scene right after adding the sun itself.

Looking at the current snippet in `world.js` that I previously edited for tone mapping, the relevant block is:

```
  sc.left = -90; sc.right = 90; sc.top = 90; sc.bottom = -90; sc.far = 320;
  scene.add(sun);
```

I need to extend this block by adding `scene.add(sun.target);` on a new line after the existing `scene.add(sun);`. I must ensure I preserve the existing code and only insert this additional line. The `replace_all` flag should be false because I'm targeting a specific occurrence, not a global replace.

Thus the edit operation will replace the exact old_string (the two lines) with a new string that includes the extra line. This will correctly attach the sun’s target to the scene, enabling the later sun-follow logic to work as intended and eliminating lighting glitches.

Proceed with the Edit tool using the specified parameters.
